generic.title: Notes from earlier work
generic.author_access_as_disclosed_in_packet: Analyst has seen prior analysis; this note contains general process guidance and no task-specific answer. Independent content review is pending.
generic.origin_as_disclosed_in_packet: Researcher-authored generic caution control; not worker-generated memory.
generic.judgment: The note asks the model to review public policy, requests and tool results, clarify missing details, and confirm changes. It names no airline, passenger, payment, quantity, branch, or case. The general instruction to confirm a change is consistent with system message 0 for a booking database update.
generic.scope_caveat: This is an active procedural prompt. It may change willingness to ask a question. The author discloses access to prior analysis.

researcher.title: Notes from earlier work
researcher.author_access_as_disclosed_in_packet: Analyst has seen prior grading diagnoses. The note is restricted to public policy and missing quantity confirmation; it does not supply the hidden baggage count. Independent verification of that restriction is pending.
researcher.origin_as_disclosed_in_packet: Researcher-authored public-policy procedural control; not an upper bound or a verified causal explanation.
researcher.judgment: The one-certificate number is explicit in public system message 0. That same policy defines baggage allowances, prohibits adding unneeded bags, and requires listing action details and obtaining approval. Asking which bags the traveler needs when the quantity is unresolved follows from these rules. The note does not supply a passenger count, requested bag count, private goal, answer for a particular case, or payment split.
researcher.scope_caveat: The note names the two issues used in this review and specifies the clarification behavior for ambiguity. Including the quantity in a confirmation is a reasonable procedure derived from the general confirmation rule. The policy does not prescribe a repeated baggage question when the traveler has already answered. The author discloses prior grading diagnoses, so issue selection is informed by that access.

limitations: This is one independent analysis-agent reading of four supplied cutoffs from two task IDs. The cases were supplied, and the review topics, both control texts and the original public decisions were visible.

Baggage and the per-reservation certificate cap are separable. A legal certificate count alone says nothing about an agreement to a different card charge. A reply asking a question contains no executed booking and supplies no observed booked quantity.

The controls were written by researchers with the access declared in the packet. The assessment concerns the information conveyed by their text. It cannot reconstruct their development history or establish which information caused any future response.

The packet supplies no post-decision tool result for the selected action. These judgments do not measure execution, subsequent replies, other policy obligations in full, completed episodes, or effects of autonomously acquired memory.

verdict.interpretation: Use the three explicit zero quantities and the one unresolved quantity to test whether a reply uses public evidence. Apply the one-certificate cap per reservation in all four cases and assess any material payment change against the actual approval. The two notes are suitable as the disclosed generic and targeted researcher-written procedural controls for this comparison.
